Jordan — thanks for taking this. ClinicCo is kicking off an updated SIG-based assessment ahead of our Q1 procurement review and we need a concise provenance pack for Redwood that covers: a canonical subprocessor roster, residency (region) for any KV/cache or telemetry exports, CAIQ/SIG exceptions (if any), and evidence pointers (attestations, CA certificates, signed addenda).

High-level asks: 
- Canonical subprocessor CSV (name, function, data access level, residency region, contract link)
- Any SIG/CAIQ control exceptions and the reason (policy/technical) + expected remediation timeline
- KMS/crypto ownership for each subprocessor that touches secrets/keys
- Preferred delivery method for evidence (we can accept S3 presigned link or secure Drive share)

Target due date: can you share the canonical CSV and attachments by COB Wed 21 Oct? If there are any exceptions that require a legal addendum, flag those — we will route to procurement.

Attachments: ClinicCo_SIG_Template.xlsx (we prefilled the sheet with the controls we care about)

Thanks — Alice

Alice — thanks, we can get that over. Quick plan and a few clarifying points: 

Plan (we'll deliver by COB Wed 21 Oct):
- Canonical subprocessor_manifest_20261018.csv (CSV) with the fields you listed.
- A CAIQ/SIG response pack (redlined_SIG_v2.xlsx) that shows any deviations and compensating controls.
- KMS residency statement (kms-residency-statement.pdf) covering key management and where keys are resident.

A couple of clarifications up front so we surface the right artifacts: 
1) One subprocessor — EdgeStream (inference edge caching) — operates an ephemeral KV cache in eu-west-1 for low-latency regional inference. We classify that as a residency exception relative to US-only controls; EdgeStream encrypts data in transit and at rest and uses customer-data separation, but they do hold ephemeral keys managed via Redwood's HSM rotation. We will document this as a SIG exception and include the compensating control around ephemeral key lifecycle and rotation logs.

2) For any contract redlines (DPA/addendum) we can provide the signed DPA template. If ClinicCo needs a specific residency SLA or onshore-only handling, that will need a legal addendum and a short procurement timeline (2–3 weeks typical).

Delivery mechanism: we will share a secure Drive folder (link below) with presigned S3 fallback for very large artifacts. If you prefer a HubSpot-attached ticket for tracking, we can push everything to RC-7823.

Link (will contain artifacts after we upload): https://drive.redwood.com/s/secure/clinicco-evidence-20261018

If that plan works I will route the CSV now and Marissa will attach the technical statements.

—Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships (acting)
Redwood Inference

Alice / Jordan — attaching the technical artifacts we discussed. Highlights and callouts below.

Attachments (uploaded):
- subprocessor_manifest_20261018.csv (CSV) — includes: name, primary function, data access classification (none/metadata/pseudonymized/plaintext), residency region, contract reference, internal owner.
- redlined_SIG_v2.xlsx (Excel) — CAIQ/SIG mapping with exceptions column and compensating-control references.
- kms-residency-statement.pdf (PDF) — statement of crypto ownership plus key-handback and rotation cadence.

Callouts: 
- EdgeStream (edge inference cache): hosts ephemeral KV in eu-west-1 to support EU low-latency inference. The KV contains prompt context segments only; we never persist PII. Keys are rotated every 7 days via Redwood HSM and we maintain rotation audit logs for 90 days. We will include the rotation manifest and a sample audit log extract in the secure folder.

- Telemetry vendor (BeaconOps): telemetry ingestion is routed through our US region and then pseudonymized before being stored for analytics. There is an export pipeline to GA that is controlled via role-based access; we note this in the SIG exceptions sheet.

- No subprocessor has access to our production customer KMS master key; all subprocessor keys are scoped and wrapped under Redwood's master key. The kms-residency-statement details the wrapping and escrow process.

Next steps: we can either: (A) drop these in the Drive link and share perms to ClinicCo security, or (B) provide a presigned S3 bundle (preferred for large audit logs). Let me know which you prefer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
